world.title: UGANDA: Bishop Calls for Greater Integration of Young People in Church Programs
world.description:
Peter Masereka
The Ordinary of the Diocese of Kasese, Rt. Rev. Francis Aquirinus Kibira Kambale, has called for greater integration of young people into Church programs, spiritual formation, and leadership, saying their active participation is essential in preparing them for future roles in both the Church and the wider community.
Bishop Kibira started his pastoral visit in one of the Parishes just five days after the Plenary Assembly of the Association of Member Episcopal Conferences in Eastern Africa (AMECEA) which was conducted from 19th-26th July 2026 on the theme “AMECEA’s synodal journey with young people: building bridges for communion, hope, Justice, and good governance.” which one of the recommendations was the prioritize the youth as the present and strong hold of the Catholic Church.
He quoted a facilitator who said, “Young people are a vital part of society, and they contribute immensely through their energy, creativity, innovation and leadership,” he said, adding that their growing numbers demand greater attention from both the Church and society.”
 Delivering his homily during Holy Mass for St. Peter and Paul Kitabu Parish's 10th anniversary celebrations and confirmation on Sunday, 02nd Aug 2026, Bishop Kibira said the call to empower young people was among the key recommendations of the recently concluded Plenary.
He urged the young people to actively participate in the Church's ministries, activities, and leadership as they prepare to fulfil Christ's call to serve God and society.
Bishop Kibira strongly warned alcohol consumers against misinterpreting Jesus’ Miracle of changing water into Wine as a free ticket to drink excessively.
He said he was shocked to realize that some men drink excessive alcohol as they use the phrase that Jesus changed water into wine, thus seriously warning them and asking them to stop alcoholism but rather concentrate on the education of their children.
Mr. Robert Baluku Friday, the Principal of the Wildlife Institute, prayed that Bishop Kibira outline the Diocese's plans for establishing a medical insurance scheme for catechists, saying it would safeguard their health and enable them to carry out their pastoral mission more effectively in the service of the salvation of souls.

world.title: ZAMBIA: “Church must Remain the Voice of the Voiceless” Church Leader
world.description:
By Archdiocese of Lusaka Media and Radio Icengelo
Archbishop Alick Banda has reaffirmed that the Catholic Church exists not to seek political power but to defend the dignity of the poor, the weak and the marginalized.
Speaking during the Priestly Ordination Mass of six priests at the Cathedral of the Child Jesus on the Feast of St. John Mary Vianney, Archbishop Banda said the Church must courageously proclaim truth, justice and peace whenever human dignity is threatened.
“The Church does not seek political power or align herself with partisan interests. She must remain the voice of the voiceless and cannot remain silent whenever truth is violated, or justice is compromised,” he said.
Addressing the newly ordained priests, the Archbishop urged them to embrace holiness, humility and faithful service, reminding them that authentic priestly ministry is rooted in Christ rather than influence, prestige or wealth.
Archbishop Banda has further encouraged them to be compassionate shepherds who accompany the wounded, defend justice and proclaim the Gospel with charity and courage, saying priests are called to heal, unite and uphold the dignity of every person.
 In a different ordination in Ndola Archdiocese, nine deacons were ordained as priests on August 1, 2026, by Archbishop Benjamin Phiri at Martyrs of Uganda Parish in Luanshya.
In his homily, Archbishop Benjamin Phiri implored the newly ordained priests to remain humble and foster a strong relationship with God in their ministry.
He urged the new priests to be prayerful, stating that prayer would allow their priesthood to serve as a solid foundation for building the Kingdom of God.
Furthermore, Archbishop Phiri called on Zambians to safeguard the country's peace as the nation approaches the August 13 general elections, emphasizing that national stability should never be taken for granted.
Speaking on the same occasion, Archbishop Phiri invited Christians, political leaders, party supporters, and all people of goodwill to pray for peace before, during, and after the elections.
He urged the laity, political stakeholders, and all citizens to conduct themselves responsibly and work together to ensure the country holds free, fair, and peaceful elections.
The Archbishop stressed the importance of preserving peace, warning that failure to do so could force Zambians to flee to neighboring countries, just as citizens from other nations have sought refuge in Zambia.
 He appealed to every well-meaning Zambian to play a role in protecting the peace the country has enjoyed over the years and to refrain from actions that could trigger violence, civil unrest, or loss of life.
Meanwhile, Archbishop Phiri challenged married individuals engaged in extramarital affairs to abandon such behavior, remain faithful to their spouses, and renew the vows they made on their wedding day.
He noted that it is disappointing for someone to freely choose a life partner among many, publicly declare a lifelong commitment, and later betray that vow by pursuing other relationships.
The Archbishop described such conduct as a betrayal of the sacred institution of marriage, urging couples to honor the lifelong covenant they freely entered into before God and the Church.

science.title: Genetic links between IIIE iron meteorites and the core of the HED parent asteroid
science.description: Rocky planets formed through the differentiation of planetesimals into metal‑rich cores and silicate mantles, yet direct evidence linking these complementary reservoirs remains scarce. Here we show that IIIE irons and howardite-eucrite-diogenite (HED) meteorites are genetically linked, by integrating mineralogical, isotopic, and rare earth element (REE) analyses of the silicate-bearing Aletai IIIE meteorite. The silicates display Fe/Mn-Fe/Mg correlations, concordant oxygen isotope compositions, and strongly fractionated REE patterns consistent with those of HED meteorites. A pronounced negative Eu anomaly in orthopyroxene marks the onset of plagioclase saturation and buoyant segregation during early magma ocean crystallization, supported by thermodynamic modelling. These findings establish a genetic link between magmatic irons and differentiated achondrites, suggesting that IIIE irons and HEDs share a common genetic heritage, and providing direct physical evidence for core-mantle reservoir connections in the early Solar System. IIIE irons share geochemical characteristics with howardite-eucrite-diogenite meteorites suggesting both may have formed from differentiated planetesimal parent bodies, according to analyses on a silicate-bearing inclusion in the Aletai IIIE iron meteorite.
